description: INSERT OR ABORT has no separate PostgreSQL syntax to translate to -- aborting the statement on a constraint violation is already PostgreSQL's own default behavior -- so Rewrite just drops the OR ABORT keyword and the plain insert must still succeed normally

body: INSERT OR ABORT INTO tE{{DLID}} (id, name) VALUES (1, 'x')
SELECT name FROM tE{{DLID}} WHERE id = 1

tests.name: row inserted normally despite the dropped OR ABORT
